sliders.label: Risk tolerance
sliders.statement: Higher risk tolerance weights threat up and success odds down: as it rises, an option with more danger gain and no better odds never drops below one with less.

sliders.label: Verticality
sliders.statement: Higher verticality weights ground gained up and switches of play down: as it rises, an option that gains more ground and switches play no more never drops below one that gains less.

sliders.label: Press trigger
sliders.statement: A higher press trigger weights counter-press cover up: as it rises, an option with more teammates near where the ball could be lost never drops below one with fewer, all else equal.

sliders.label: Defensive line height
sliders.statement: A higher line weights rest defence up: as it rises, an option that leaves more of the space behind it covered never drops below one that leaves less, all else equal.

principles.text: Keep the ball: when the gain is close, take the pass most likely to arrive
Don't force the final ball; wait for the opening to appear
Move up the pitch through patient circulation rather than early balls forward
Draw the opponent to one side, then switch to the free side
Get the ball forward in few passes
principles.source: Direct play; C. Reep and B. Benjamin, "Skill and Chance in Association Football", JRSS A 131 (1968)

principles.text: Accept losing some balls in exchange for territory
Get the ball into the areas chances come from
Go for goal straight after winning the ball, before the defence is set
principles.source: Rangnick: the best time to score is within 10 seconds of winning the ball (The Athletic, 2021)

principles.text: Accept lower odds for a bigger threat while the opponent is disorganised
Play forward into the space behind the opponent
Attack the space directly instead of switching play
Win the ball back within seconds of losing it, so keep players close to where it could be lost
principles.source: Counter-pressing: Guardiola's Barcelona (2008-12), five-to-six-second rule; Rangnick's eight-second rule

principles.text: A high line leaves space behind it, so keep cover behind the ball in case the move breaks down
Press straight away only when teammates are close to the loss; otherwise regroup
Keep a balanced shape behind the ball
Drop into shape after losing the ball rather than pressing it
A deep line leaves little space behind it, so a turnover in front of it costs less
